findings.text: The no-usable-lane refusal is now built from resolution.competence, which plan §16 forbids ('Never build this refusal from routing._competence_verdict'): that verdict can report the resolved lane within its window and then carry no shortfall. Nothing here asserts the stored verdict's context block actually refused the lane, so when it reports allowed, CompetenceLimit.__init__ (reckon/crew/node.py:615-620) takes its non-context branch and reads competence_horizon_hours, raising KeyError instead of the exit-5 context refusal the done_when requires. The divergence is reachable because _reroute_oversized_request censuses with no backend settings (a codex standing chain) while _context_fit_verdict measures the resolved backend's own chain. The added parity assertion covers only the agreeing case.

The reviewed run's manifest still carries no rubric.<dimension> line for any of the six review dimensions, so a reader cannot tell whether the worker checked the delivered work against the rubric; the same gap was raised at 055f8161da and is unchanged.
